body.br:
SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1170.091.(Currently Amended) An air-permeable bedding system, comprising:
a microclimate fabric layer; and
an air-permeable capacitive sensor layer below the microclimate fabric layer, the air- permeable capacitive sensor layer comprises a top two air-permeable substrate[[s]] and a bottom air-permeable substrate, wherein the top air-permeable each substrate carries a top set of electrically conductive pathways and the bottom air-permeable substrate carries a bottom set ofelectronically conductive pathways, the top set and the bottom set being arranged at an angle ofeach other, the electrically conductive pathways in the top set being configured to be spaced apart from each other to form a top set ofhorizontal air pathways and the electrically conductive pathways in the bottom set being configured to be spaced apart from each other to form a bottom set ofhorizontal air pathways, the two top and bottom sets of electrically conductive pathways separated vertically by an air- permeable dielectric layer that is located between the top and bottom two air- permeable substrates, wherein the air-permeable dielectric layer defines a horizontal air pathway allowing for airflow horizontally between the two sets of electrically conductive pathways, wherein the two top and bottom air-permeable substrates respectively securely position the two top and bottom sets of electrically conductive pathways to cross over each other forming a grid, forming capacitors at intersection points ofthe grid, and forming vertical air-pathways at a plurality ofgaps ofthe grid,the intersection points defining a sensor grid, wherein
the sensor grid comprises a plurality of gaps that define a plurality of vertical air pathways, and wherein the dielectric layer and the two top and bottom air- permeable substrates comprise cut-outs at the vertical air pathways such that airflow passes vertically through the plurality of gaps [[in]] of the sensor grid and horizontally through the air-permeable dielectric layer.
2. (Canceled)
3. (Currently Amended) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, wherein the top air-permeable substrate[[s]] and bottom air-permeable substrate are formed from meshes or foam.
4. (Currently Amended) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, wherein at least one of the electrically conductive pathways carried by one of the top and bottom air- permeable substrates is encapsulated by a thermoplastic.
5. (Currently Amended) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 4, wherein the thermoplastic is bonded to the one of the top and bottom air-permeable substrates.
6. (Currently Amended) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 5, wherein the thermoplastic is bonded to the one of the top and bottom air-permeable substrates by heat lamination.
7. (Original) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
a foam comfort layer between the microclimate fabric layer and the air-permeable capacitive sensor layer.
8. (Original) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
a piezoelectric sensor below the microclimate fabric layer.
9. (Original) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 8, further comprising a transmitter configured to transmit signals of the capacitive sensor layer for determining a respiration rate and to transmit signals of the piezoelectric sensor for determining a heart rate.
10. (Original) The air-permeable bedding system of claim 1, further comprising:
an inlet configured to be connected to an active air source that increases airflow within the air-permeable bedding system.
11. (Withdrawn) A computer-implemented method, comprising:
receiving pressure sensor data from a bedding system that comprises a sensor grid that generates the pressure sensor data;
identifying, based on the pressure sensor data, a target body part of a person on the bedding system;
identifying a subset of the pressure sensor data generated from a region of the sensor grid that measures pressure exerted by the target body part; and
using the subset of the pressure sensor data to determine a heart rate or a respiration rate of the person.
12. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein identifying, based on the pressure sensor data, the target body part of the person on the bedding system comprises:
identifying the person's body and joint positions of the person using the pressure sensor data, andApplication No.: 17/019,090 identifying the target body part based on the joint positions.
13. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 12, wherein identifying the person's body and target joint positions of the person using the pressure sensor data comprises:
arranging the pressure sensor data as a matrix of pressure data, and
inputting the matrix of pressure data to a machine learning model for identifying the target joint positions.
14. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein using the subset of the pressure sensor data to determine the heart rate or the respiration rate of the person comprises:
calculating an average pressure corresponding to the region based on the subset of the pressure sensor data,
generating a time series of pressure readings corresponding to the region, and
determining the heart rate or the respiration rate based on the time series.
15. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 11, wherein the target body part is a lumbar area of the person.
16. (Withdrawn) A computer-implemented method, comprising:
receiving a time series of pressure sensor data from a bedding system that comprises a sensor grid that generates the pressure sensor data;
identifying poses of a person on the bedding system based on the pressure sensor data;
determining respiration rates of the person based on the pressure sensor data; andApplication No.: 17/019,090 inputting the poses and the respiration rates of the person to a machine learning model to determine a sleep state of the person.
17. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein identifying the poses of the person on the bedding system based on the pressure sensor data comprises:
arranging, for a particular instance in time, the pressure sensor data as a matrix of pressure readings,
inputting the matrix of pressure readings to a machine learning model for a particular pose at the particular instance, and
generating other poses in other instances in time using the machine learning model.
18. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein the poses and the respiration rates are formatted as two additional time series.
19. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 16, wherein the sleep state is one of candidate sleep states, and the machine learning model generates a probability that the person is in a particular candidate sleep state for each candidate state, the sleep state selected being the particular candidate sleep state with the highest probability.
20. (Withdrawn) The computer-implemented method of claim 16, further comprising:
determining heart rates of the person, wherein the machine learning model also receives the heart rates to determine the sleep state of the person.
